text: v1 of Promises stores everything in browser localStorage only, with no sync, by explicit choice of the owner to keep it simple. The owner wants cross-device sync via a server later. Plan discussed for that step: a Yjs document on the client, the y-websocket provider, and a small self-hosted Hocuspocus server with its SQLite extension, one process serving static files plus WebSocket, access by unguessable list URL. Keep the storage code behind one module so this swap stays contained.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: Rejected for sync (2026-10): (1) Peer-only WebRTC via y-webrtc: its default public signaling servers are mostly dead. (2) Trystero (WebRTC with Nostr/BitTorrent discovery) plus a custom Yjs adapter: works with no server, but devices only sync while both are open at the same time. (3) Iroh: no browser npm package (needs a custom Rust-to-WASM wrapper crate), and in browsers all traffic goes through n0 relays, whose free public tier is for hobby use only; gossip also needs a known bootstrap peer. The owner chose a real server later instead of any of these.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: Owner decisions for v1 (2026-10): open promises can deliberately NOT be edited or deleted, and broken ones cannot be removed; this is the point of the app, not a missing feature. Kept promises leave the list at local midnight of the day they were kept and then only count. Undo for keeping exists only on the Kept screen right after keeping. Yjs was deferred until sync is added; v1 stores plain JSON. Hall subtitle spells numbers below thirteen as words.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: Owner prefers terse UI copy that does not explain the mechanics (30 days of ink, fading, the hall). Explainers on the Make and List screens were cut to 'You'd better keep your promise(s).', and all day countdowns ('N days of ink left', 'N days left', 'with N days of ink to spare') were removed from the list and kept screens. The fading visuals carry the meaning; avoid adding explanatory or countdown copy back.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>

text: PWA (2026-10): the owner installs Promises on both iPhone and Android home screens, and the site is hosted on Cloudflare Pages. Pages' default Cache-Control (max-age=0, must-revalidate) is why there is no _headers file for sw.js. Deliberately not built in v1: an in-app 'new version' prompt (updates auto-reload instead), an install banner, and push/deadline reminders (would need a server, and iOS needs the app installed first). iOS home-screen apps have storage separate from Safari, so promises do not carry over between them until sync exists.
author: Stavros Korokithakis <hi@stavros.io>
